findings.F1: The book's deepest fall was -83% (Calmar 0.14), running from w12 through w21 over 1,051 days; the book summed -0.870 in daily returns while holding the coins summed +0.505. Windows w12, w13, w16 and w18 alone summed -0.342, -0.299, -0.199 and -0.493, against holding's -0.027, -0.125, +0.544 and +0.013.
findings.F2: While long, the position's daily gain rose steadily with the coin's past 20-bar return. By quartile of that return (2,035 bars each) the mean daily gain was -0.00034 (t -0.41), 0.00087 (t 1.04), 0.00196 (t 1.64) and 0.00691 (t 3.04). The top quartile alone carried 14.07 of the summed gain of 19.12.
findings.F3: While long, the bottom quartile of the past 60-bar return (mean -23%, n 1,267) lost -0.00070 a day (t -2.78). Every other quartile gained between 0.0025 and 0.0042 a day.
findings.F4: Long days with a negative past 20-bar return earned nothing: -0.00049 a day (n 3,145) when more than 10% below the 60-bar high, and -0.00042 (n 1,568) when near it. Long days with a positive past 20-bar return earned 0.0037 (t 2.06) and 0.0043 (t 3.08).
findings.F5: In the four losing windows the book was long mostly on falling coins. The median past 60-bar return was -8.2% against +20.8% elsewhere, and the median fall from the 60-bar high was -22% against -8%. There, long days with a negative past 20-bar return lost -0.0066 a day (t -2.82, n 932), while those with a positive one lost only -0.0016 (t -0.82, n 671).
findings.F6: The forecast's own grading adds little. By quartile of the raw distance above the 200-day average, the long daily gain moved from 0.00027 (t 1.38) to 0.0045 (t 1.89). In the 20-bar test, the forecast 0-5 and 5-10 buckets had excess returns of -0.029 and -0.011, and only 42% of active bars beat holding.
findings.F7: The book was long on 56% of days, and the coin rose 0.00087 a day on the days it stood flat. Being out of the market therefore cost the book about as much as holding earned, which pushed its Sharpe 0.065 below holding's.

ideas.idea: While a coin's close sits above its long moving average, the coin keeps rising in proportion to how far above it the close sits, only while the coin's own recent return over the past several weeks is positive; the more it has risen over those weeks, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold a coin that sits above its long average only while its recent weeks are rising, sized by that rise, and step out when it trades above the average but is falling, which removes the losing long days that made the book's deepest fall.
ideas.name: above-average trend with momentum

ideas.idea: While a coin's close sits above its long moving average, the coin keeps rising in proportion to how far above it the close sits, except when the close has fallen far below its recent high, in which case the deeper that fall, the weaker the rise that follows.
ideas.consequence: A trader would cut a long on a coin above its long average as the coin falls from its recent high, so the book is not long through the drawdowns that carried its losing windows.
ideas.name: above-average trend near highs

ideas.idea: (new idea) A coin's return over the following weeks grows with its own return over the past several weeks, whatever the coin's position against its long moving average, so the stronger the recent rise, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size a long by the coin's recent multi-week return rather than by its distance from the long average, staying in rising coins that the long average leaves flat.
ideas.name: multi-week momentum persists
